head_commit.message:
chore(pool): declare onepipeline-ui's pool maintenance (#335)

## What

Declare onevcs maintenance for idle warm-pool slots using
`cargo-prune-superseded` 0.1.1, installed by bootstrap. Cleanup removes
superseded Cargo builds older than two days while preserving each unit’s
newest build and all recent builds.

Add a 20-second steady-state maintenance budget, checked after the
release-PR quality gate. Expensive measurement stays outside per-change
checks; cheap journeys cover cleanup, reporting and failure behavior.

## Why

Superseded build output across the host’s pool reached about 926 GB and
nearly filled a 1.8 TB disk twice in four days. Repository-owned cleanup
reclaims obsolete output while keeping builds warm. The budget bounds
how long regular maintenance holds a slot out of service.

## Additional info

The only dependency change in `Cargo.lock` is `rustls` 0.23.45 →
0.23.46, addressing the advisories reported by the required deny check
(RUSTSEC-2026-0346 through RUSTSEC-2026-0349). The incidental change to
`tempfile`’s `getrandom` dependency was reverted; no other locked
dependency moves.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nick DeRobertis <19440155+nickderobertis@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(deps): resolve onevcs 0.51.3 beside the linked engine

Move the test-only `onevcs` requirement to `=0.51.3`, the release whose
boundary stops reading generic words as test words, and move the lock's
single onevcs resolution with it. The linked engine stays `=0.72.0`; its
caret on onevcs 0.51.2 accepts 0.51.3, so the tree keeps one copy of each.
No route, payload or UI changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(deps): align the API with the generic test-word engine (#339)

## What

Align the dev-only onevcs pin and the linked engine’s shared resolution
on 0.51.3, keeping one copy of each dependency. The base already pins
onepipeline to 0.72.0, so its version and public semver class remain
unchanged. No UI, HTTP route, journal-shape or unrelated dependency
changes.

## Why

Browser-adopted runs use the API’s compiled engine as their driver.
Keeping its dependency resolution aligned with the host completes the
dependency alignment for the generic-word boundary fix.

Co-authored-by: Nick DeRobertis <19440155+nickderobertis@users.noreply.github.com>

head_commit.message:
feat(deps)!: link the engine with supervised manager landings (#337)

## What

Relink to published onepipeline 0.72.0 and align `/healthz` with that
engine. Adopt its significance-aware `planner` profile and matchers, and
align browser reply validation and timeline categories with its
vocabulary. Update locked rustls to 0.23.46 and fix Windows compilation
of the planner-parity journey.

## Why

Browser adoption can retain its own linked engine as a driver. Matching
that engine to the CLI preserves supervision of manager-started landings
through either entry point and lets hosts verify engine version
equality.

## Additional info

Breaking Rust API dependency move: engine types exposed through
`ApiError::from_engine`, `EventFilter::to_engine`, and
`telemetry::of_run` now belong to onepipeline 0.72.0. The public matcher
also gains `significance`.

The `planner` profile includes producer-stamped VCS milestones and
blockers and excludes pipeline progress. A real-server journey compares
that selection with the linked engine and checks rejection of invalid
significance values. The browser recognizes `readjust` envelopes without
adding a composer shortcut or landing routes.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nick DeRobertis <19440155+nickderobertis@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat(deps)!: link the engine that supervises manager landings

Pin the linked engine to onepipeline =0.72.0 and the test-only onevcs to
=0.51.2, the release that engine's own lock resolves; the lock follows the
engine's to oneagentgraph 0.5.7, so the embedded engine links the same
siblings as the `onepipeline` CLI `just bootstrap` provisions.

On the manager's ruling, adopt the engine's shared filter grammar and
shipped `planner` profile (onepipeline docs/contract.md, entry 123):
`?filter=` matchers accept `significance`, and `planner` is read from the
engine's `Filters::profile` rather than a hand copy. docs/contract.md states
both and names onepipeline's contract as their authority. This crate
classifies no event's significance itself.

Browser vocabulary follows the engine's drift gates: the `readjust` reply
command is spelled by the grammar but offered as no shortcut, and the
landing, absorb, readjust and change-closed/reopened kinds are filed under
timeline categories.

BREAKING CHANGE: The engine moves from 0.71 to 0.72.
`ApiError::from_engine`, `filter::EventFilter::to_engine` and
`telemetry::of_run` expose engine types, so Rust consumers must align with
the new engine line. `filter::Matcher` gains a public `significance` field,
and the `planner` profile now admits stamped `vcs` milestones and blockers
and drops pipeline records stamped progress.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
